title: Consensus and Byzantine Fault Tolerance for Agents

questions.question: Five agents vote, but three share a base model and give the same wrong answer. Why may majority voting fail?
options: Majority voting requires all responses to be numeric
The vote count is too large for a semantic cluster
The result is invalid unless each agent has a different name
Their errors are correlated, so the majority is not independent evidence
questions.explanation: Majority vote treats each ballot as another piece of evidence, but agents sharing a base model can share the same hallucination. Distinct agent names do not make those errors independent, so a three-agent false cluster can outvote correct dissent.

questions.question: What fault bound does classical PBFT state for a system with n nodes and f Byzantine nodes?
options: f must be less than n divided by 3
f must be greater than n divided by 2
f may equal n if messages are signed
f is unrelated to the number of nodes
questions.explanation: Classical PBFT assumes fewer than one third of nodes are Byzantine: f < n/3, equivalently at least 3f+1 nodes for f faults. A bound above one half is too permissive for the protocol’s stated quorum guarantee.

questions.question: How does CP-WBFT alter a simple one-vote-per-agent tally?
options: It removes all votes from agents that disagree
It waits for a leader to produce an unrelated answer
It weights each answer using an attached confidence probe
It selects the answer with the longest explanation
questions.explanation: CP-WBFT attaches a confidence probe to each answer and sums confidence by semantic answer cluster. Removing every dissenting vote is not weighting; it discards evidence instead of adjusting each cluster’s contribution.

questions.question: What does the lesson describe as the key robust aggregation idea in DecentLLMs?
options: Average every answer string character by character
Allow the first agent to decide the answer for all others
Score parallel proposals and use a geometric-median-style aggregation
Give the highest-confidence agent permanent control
questions.explanation: DecentLLMs has workers propose in parallel, evaluators score those proposals, and a geometric-median-style rule aggregates them to resist outliers. Giving one high-confidence agent permanent control is leader-based selection, not the described robust aggregation.

questions.question: All agents agree on a factual answer, but no independent source or test has checked it. What does consensus establish?
options: That the agents' errors are uncorrelated
Correctness, if the group has at least three members
An independent proof of every cited premise
Agreement among agents, not necessarily correctness
questions.explanation: Consensus establishes that agents agree, not that they independently checked a fact or that the fact is true. A minimum group size cannot repair correlated hallucinations; external evidence or an independent verifier is still needed.

questions.question: A confidence-weighted winning cluster fails the configured acceptance threshold. What should the protocol do?
options: Let the most confident agent rewrite the votes
Lower the threshold after seeing the preferred answer
Discard minority clusters and report certainty
Retry or escalate rather than accept a weak majority
questions.explanation: The protocol accepts only when the leading cluster’s weight clears the configured fraction of total confidence; below that it retries or escalates. Lowering the threshold after seeing a favored answer changes the acceptance rule to fit the outcome.
